info.title: Documentation for your Premium plan
info.description:
This interactive documentation lets you try real API requests. Select an endpoint on the left and read its description for details about the available parameters. Click `Test Request` to open the interactive API client, fill in the parameters, and press `Send` to view a full API response. You can then inspect the JSON response, copy the `curl` command to run it on your machine, or obtain a URL of the request.
The Meteosource API is a RESTful API. Requests are made with `GET` and query parameters; responses are JSON-encoded, except where noted (e.g. the weather map endpoints return `image/png`). ### Base URL The base URL for this documentation is `https://www.meteosource.com/api/v1/premium`. ### Authentication Requests are authenticated with your unique API key, supplied in one of these ways: * the `key` query parameter * the `X-API-Key` header * the `Authorization: Bearer ` header Specifying the `key` query parameter together with either header is rejected with a `403` error, as is specifying none of them. If both headers are present, `X-API-Key` takes precedence and `Authorization` is ignored. You can find and manage your API key in [your dashboard](https://www.meteosource.com/client). ### Errors The API returns standard HTTP status codes. Error responses include a JSON body with a `detail` field describing the problem: ```json { "detail": "explanation of what went wrong" } ``` Common error codes: `400` (invalid parameter), `402` (daily request limit exceeded), `403` (API key missing, invalid, or specified twice), `429` (per-minute rate limit exceeded). ### Pagination The Meteosource API does not use pagination - all results for a request are returned at once. ### Important notes * For a detailed description of the response variables, consult the response `Schema` * Don't assume a fixed set or order of variables and sections - new ones may be added over time. Always check a field is present before using it. * The response includes an `Expires` header marking when the data will next change. Use it to avoid unnecessary requests and improve your app's performance. * HTTP compression is supported - add an `Accept-Encoding: gzip` header to enable it.

get.description:
## Current weather and forecast for single location

### Sections
The endpoint can return multiple sections of data. To obtain the best performance, we advise only requesting the sections you actually need. The available sections are as follows:

* Current weather situation
* Hourly forecast (for 24/48/96/168 hours, depending on the tier)
* Daily forecast (for 7/10/30 days, depending on the tier)
* Minutely precipitation forecast (for 60 minutes in the following hour, only for higher tiers)
* Weather alerts (only for higher tiers)

By default, only the current and hourly sections are returned. The division into daily parts (morning, afternoon and evening) is only available for the first 7 days of the forecast. For details regarding available parameters, see the parameter description below.

### Notes
* Variables can be instantaneous, averaged, or accumulated over certain time. For example, `precipitation` forecast provides the precipitation accumulated until the next hour (data with timestamp as `12:00:00` is rain accumulated from `12:00:00` to `13:00:00`).
* The detailed description of weather alerts is only available in English. The alert category is translated into selected language.

parameters.name: sections

schema.description:
Sections to be included in the response. You can specify more section by separating the values with a comma. The available values are:

* ``current``: Current weather situation
* ``daily``: Forecasts for each whole day, without the daily parts
* ``daily-parts``: Forecasts for each whole day, morning, afternoon and evening
    * Important: forecast for the morning, afternoon and evening is available only for the first
      7 days in the forecast
* ``hourly``: Forecasts with hourly resolution
* ``minutely``: Precipitation forecast with 1 minute resolution
* ``alerts``: The weather alerts
* ``all``: All sections

parameters.name: timezone

schema.description:
Timezone to be used for the date fields. If not specified, local timezone of the forecast location will be used.
The format is according to the tzinfo database, so values like `Europe/Prague` or `UTC` can be used.
Alternatively you may use the value ``auto`` in which case the local timezone of the location is used.
The full list of valid timezone strings can be found [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones#List).

get.description:
Get weather data for a single location (specified either by geographic coordinates or by a place ID) and a given day in the past.

### Sections
The response is split into following sections:

* `data`: Actual hourly weather records for the requested day, available up to 20 years in the past.
* `daily`: Daily summary (average, minimum, and maximum) computed from that same day's hourly records in `data`.
* `statistics`: Long-term climate normals for this calendar day (e.g. every August 14th, regardless of year) - typical averages plus all-time record extremes, computed from around 40 years of historical data.

get.description:
You can use this endpoint to obtain `place_id` of the location you want, to be used in the [Weather](#tag/weather) endpoints.
The response also contains detailed information about the location, such as coordinates, timezone and the country the place belongs to.

Unlike the [Search for places by prefix](#tag/locations/GET/find_places_prefix) endpoint, complete words are required here. You can search for cities,
mountains, lakes, countries, ZIP codes, etc. The response can contain multiple places, sorted by relevance.
You can then identify the one you want by coordinates, country, or the administrative area.

get.description:
Get PNG weather forecast maps for given area and variable ### Area specification There are two ways to specify geographical area you need for your map: 1. Specify `X` and `Y` coordinates and zoom level `Z` of desired tile in Google Maps Tile notation. 2. Specify latitude and longitude bounds of the area you want to cover. ### Notes * The resulting PNG maps are **always** in Google Mercator projection (EPSG:3857). * As Meteosource only covers areas between latitudes 80° and -80°, you can only request maps within these bounds, when specifying the latitude and longitude boundaries. When specifying the area using Google Maps Tile notation, the regions outside our supported latitudes will be fully transparent. * The finest resolution is not available for maps covering very large regions. The resulting map will be automatically downscaled in this case, to guarantee high-speed responses. * Weather maps are only supported for forecasts, not for archive data. ### Color maps Below you will find color maps for each variable that you can use as a legend for your map. You can also download [numerical references](https://www.meteosource.com/static/files/colormaps.zip) for the color maps. **`temperature`** (unit: `°C`)
**`feels_like_temperature`** (unit: `°C`)
**`clouds`** (unit: `%`)
**`precipitation`** (unit: `mm/h`)
**`wind_speed`** (unit: `m/s`)
**`wind_gust`** (unit: `m/s`)
**`pressure`** (unit: `hPa`)
**`humidity`** (unit: `%`)
**`wave_height`** (unit: `m`)
**`wave_period`** (unit: `s`)
**`sea_temperature`** (unit: `°C`)
**`air_quality`** (unit: `Index`)
**`ozone_surface`** (unit: `µg/m³`)
**`ozone_total`** (unit: `Dobson`)
**`no2`** (unit: `µg/m³`)
**`pm2.5`** (unit: `µg/m³`)

* `temperature`: Temperature 2 metres above ground
* `feels_like_temperature`: Feels like temperature
* `clouds`: Percentage of sky covered by clouds
* `precipitation`: Total precipitation amount accumulated since last hour
* `wind_speed`: Wind speed 10 metres above the ground
* `wind_gust`: Wind gust speed
* `pressure`: Atmospheric pressure at mean sea level
* `humidity`: Relative humidity
* `wave_height`: Wave height
* `wave_period`: Wave period
* `sea_temperature`: Sea temperature (available only for +-24 hours)
* `air_quality`: Air quality index
* `ozone_surface`: Ozone at surface level
* `ozone_total`: Total column ozone
* `no2`: Nitrogen dioxide at surface level
* `pm2.5`: Particulate matter d < 2.5 µm (PM2.5)

type.description:
The character of the place. May be one of the following values:

* administrative areas (states, counties, districts...): ``administrative_area``
* country: ``country``
* a different political entity from a country (for example, a dependent teritory): ``political_entity``
* villages, towns and cities: ``settlement``
* air industry locations: ``airbase``, ``airfield``, ``heliport``, ``airport``, ``airport_terminal``
* places related to water: ``bay``, ``channel``, ``fjord``, ``lake``, ``pond``, ``falls``, ``gulf``,
    ``harbor``, ``reservoir``, ``sea``, ``dam``, ``cape``, ``island``, ``peninsula``
* places related to mountain areas: ``hill``, ``mountain``, ``peak``, ``valley``, ``volcano``, ``canyon``
* other places related to nature: ``park``, ``reserve``, ``resort``, ``desert``
* places based on postcodes: ``postcode``

data.description:
Array of active weather alerts for the location, sorted by severity.
An empty array means there are no active alerts for the location.

tags.name: Weather
tags.description:
This section contains endpoints for retrieving current, forecast, and historical weather data for a single [location](#tag/locations).

For every endpoint in this section, location is a required parameter (some endpoints also
require other parameters, e.g. `date`), and can be specified in one of two ways:

1. GPS coordinates, using the `lat` and `lon` parameters.
2. **OR** A place name, using the `place_id` parameter. Obtain a `place_id` from one of the endpoints in the [Locations](#tag/locations) section in this API documentation.

### Notes
* When daylight saving time starts, one hourly record will be missing (typically `2:00:00 AM`). When daylight saving time ends, the hourly data will contain two records with duplicate times (typically `2:00:00 AM`).
* For mountains, it is usually better to specify the `place_id` rather than the `lat` and `lon`. When you use `place_id`, you are guaranteed to receive data for the precise elevation of the peak. When you specify the coordinates, the elevation can be less precise.
* **Weather icon fields** (e.g. `status_num`) return a numeric code; see the [`WeatherIconCode`](#models/WeatherIconCode) schema description for the full mapping of codes to their icon names and descriptions.
